Archstone Security · Research · FedRAMP

FedRAMP 20x agency adoption, by the numbers.

FedRAMP has issued 34 20x authorizations in the 452 days since the first, on Jul 25, 2025. 3 of them have an agency authorization from anyone other than the FedRAMP PMO, which records one on every 20x listing. Of the 13 held by GRC and compliance-automation vendors, zero have an agency customer.

Those figures understate the program. GRC and compliance-automation vendors are heavily over-represented: they hold 13 of the 34 20x authorizations (38%). By the category providers choose for their own listings, GRC tools are 24% of 20x authorizations against 5% of Rev5 authorizations issued over the same period. None of those 13 has an agency customer. Agencies do buy GRC tools — all 8 GRC products authorized the traditional way have an agency behind them — just not through 20x, where the wave of GRC listings tracks vendors selling 20x readiness more than agency demand. Set the GRC vendors aside and 3 of the remaining 21 have an agency (14%), not 9%. The adoption 20x does have is AI platforms: ChatGPT Enterprise and API Platform, Gemini for Government and Perplexity Enterprise and API Platform. It is narrow: three agencies, one of them on all three. Even at 14%, 20x remains far from the traditional path, where every agency-path authorization starts with a sponsor.

20x changes where in the process certification is granted but doesn't shorten the adoption timeline.

Every row starts on the day the product's marketplace listing entered the process. The grey bar runs to its 20x authorization; the dashed line runs from there to today. The shaded band is where a Rev5 authorization usually lands, middle half of products, measured the same way from the listing date. A Rev5 agency-path authorization comes with its sponsoring agency, so it is the point where an agency is relying on the product. For 20x that point has not arrived.

How these numbers are made

  • Source. The FedRAMP Marketplace's own JSON export, downloaded on a schedule and kept as dated snapshots. The page is rebuilt whenever the export changes.
  • Agency ATO means an agency other than the FedRAMP PMO listed on the product. The PMO records an agency use on every 20x authorization, so the marketplace's own authorization count shows at least one for every 20x product. That entry is removed everywhere on this page.
  • Authorization date is the marketplace's certification date for the product. The export lists the agencies on each product but not the date each agency signed, so this measures reliance as it stands today, not when it happened.
  • Business categories. The marketplace export for Oct 20, 2026 dropped the business categories from most listings at once. Where a listing has no category in that export, the category it carried in the latest earlier snapshot (Oct 16, 2026) is used (359 listings). A listing whose category changed to a different one is not affected.
  • GRC and compliance vendors are identified from a separately maintained provider classification feed (data as of Oct 16, 2026), matched by provider name, and shown alongside the GRC business category providers choose for their own marketplace listings.
  • AI platforms are identified from a short provider list maintained alongside the GRC feed and applied to 20x products only. The marketplace's own "Artificial Intelligence (AI)" category is not used here: several AI products, including ChatGPT and Gemini, are not tagged with it.
  • Reclassification. No 20x record in the current export carries status history from before 2025 or an agency ATO inherited from a Rev5 authorization. Products authorized on both tracks are noted under the objections table; their agencies count toward Rev5. A listing that is only FedRAMP Ready on one track is not counted as a match, since Ready is not an authorization. Snapshots are kept so that a record converted in place will show up when two exports are compared.
  • Track labels for new listings. Listings in the Initial Implementation intake status carry a Rev5 or 20x label that does not always match the program the provider is pursuing, and at least one provider is listed twice, once on each track. Authorized products and agency ATOs are not affected; counts of products still in process should be read as approximate.
  • Limits. Withdrawn and expired products are not in the export. Class A 20x entries without an authorization date are included in totals and left out of anything plotted by date.
